kept.heading: HOW TO PLAN 2027 WHEN TRAFFIC IS DOWN AND AI WON'T ATTRIBUTE (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Build the 2027 marketing plan around AI visibility, brand mentions, community participation, branded search, and other signals that happen before a website visit. Start by identifying which AI engines, communities, publications, and sources influence buyers in your category, then budget specific hours and owners for digital PR, off site content, community work, and proprietary research. Measure exposure, branded search, and business outcomes together each month because no single metric captures influence when attribution is incomplete. Fund proven tactics at full capacity, cap new experiments with clear owners and kill dates, and reallocate the budget each quarter based on what the three layer measurement shows.
kept.article_text:
Title: How to plan 2027 when traffic is down and AI won't attribute

URL Source: https://www.growth-memo.com/p/how-to-plan-2027-when-traffic-is

Published Time: 2026-10-05T20:31:05+00:00

Markdown Content:
[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!aeCc!,w_2400,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F9a839721-93f4-42d6-a7d4-c6457ae1e1aa_1672x941.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!aeCc!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F9a839721-93f4-42d6-a7d4-c6457ae1e1aa_1672x941.png)

This Memo was sent to 29,512 subscribers. Welcome to +88 new readers! Sign up for free to get new insights every week, or sign up for Premium to get exclusive tools and frameworks that make you more effective.

It’s planning season! And like every year, most execs start by setting a traffic target that breaks down into revenue. But depending on what industry they work in, that doesn’t make sense anymore for most brands.

Last November, we wrote that[SEO budgets buy capacity](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/budget-seo-for-capacity-not-output) and that click-based ROI had decayed. A week later, we argued that[leadership buys controlled learning](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/selling-ai-search-strategies-to-leadership) when certainty is off the table. Both couldn’t be more relevant today.

So what changed for your 2027 planning? How much of the work now happens where no click, cookie, or referral can see it?

Plan 2027 around the signals that happen before the visit… or despite it.

The November 2025 memo made 2 calls: Most **SEO costs are fixed** (salaries, tools, infrastructure), so the budget question is which capabilities to fund. And the split should come from **scenarios instead of last year’s traffic**. For example, 40% of capacity goes to [digital PR](https://library.growth-memo.com/p/digital-pr), 30% to technical SEO, 20% to content operations, and 10% to research, adjusted by priority and weak spots. We also advised pitching tests and experiments that were well planned, had firm boundaries, and kill switches if they weren’t producing results.

Keeping all that in mind, 3 things have moved since then:

*   Zero-click searches rose from 60.45% of US Google searches in 2024 to 68.01% in early 2026, per[SparkToro and Similarweb data](https://searchengineland.com/google-zero-click-searches-2026-study-479717). Roughly 2 in 3 searches now end without a visit, so a traffic baseline is doomed to shrink and undercount visibility before 2027 even starts.

*   AI tools moved into marketing teams as unbudgeted build time.[Part 1 of the AI marketing automation](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/the-ai-hours-nobody-on-your-marketing) series argues those hours often come straight out of brand work.

*   Attribution broke past the point of repair.[Graphite estimates](https://growth-memo.com/p/the-collapse-of-attribution) AI can be underattributed by 10x. _Yikes_. That means a plan developed on what can be cleanly attributed will cut resources from the channels that work.

A buyer can [read an AI answer](https://library.growth-memo.com/p/generative-ai-search), scan a Reddit thread, and see a peer’s LinkedIn post about your product before visiting your site once. In years past, planning for organic visibility treated the visit as the first measurable moment—or the ideal one. In 2027, most of the influence will land earlier.

Look at this search journey for buying a Samsung TV, measured in [Semrush](https://www.semrush.com/lp/journeys/en/), for example.

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ngeb!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F945d3997-b290-4117-880f-5f42e2bb7541_2048x1562.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ngeb!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F945d3997-b290-4117-880f-5f42e2bb7541_2048x1562.png)

Or this one, of a user buying a foundation from Sephora.

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!fXcZ!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F2ed9a236-acac-4168-a72c-f1a0fc2986df_2048x1600.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!fXcZ!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F2ed9a236-acac-4168-a72c-f1a0fc2986df_2048x1600.png)

Disjointed. Messy. The [Messy Middle](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/messy-middle)!

And so far in 2026, [only about 1/3 of searches](https://sparktoro.com/blog/in-2026-less-than-one-third-of-google-searches-still-send-a-click/) produce any kind of click, according to Sparktoro. But the [visits are still happening](https://library.growth-memo.com/p/validation-click); they might just show up in the wrong column.

SparkToro and[Similarweb tracked clickstream behavior](https://sparktoro.com/blog/new-research-from-similarweb-how-ai-brand-mentions-influence-direct-visits-traditional-search-queries/) for 7 days after AI recommended Capital One: Direct visits to those brands rose, while search visits ran about 15% lower, and the lift reached 14.2%. (So your dashboard that reads direct traffic as “unknown” or uncategorized is likely counting AI influence as noise.)

I chatted about this recently with my colleague and friend, [Amanda Natividad](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amandanat/), VP of Marketing at SparkToro and author of _[Zero Click Marketing](https://zeroclickmarketing.co/)_, who puts the planning consequence plainly:

> _“If people are increasingly getting answers without clicking, then you need to plan for the signals that happen before, or instead of, the visit. That means prioritizing things like brand mentions, citations, discussions about your brand, and participation in the communities where your audience already hangs out.”_

Those signals are spread thin across surfaces, with the [AI citation](https://library.growth-memo.com/p/ai-citation-brand-citation)/[AI mention](https://library.growth-memo.com/p/ai-mentions-brand-mentions) overlap between engines being minuscule: [91% of citations appear in only one](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/ai-halftime-report-h1-2026) of ChatGPT, Perplexity, or AI Overviews. So presence has to be planned surface by surface, much like social platforms.

[![Image 4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!PSVb!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fbc2b5e08-aac0-467e-b969-29c06504b700_900x450.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!PSVb!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fbc2b5e08-aac0-467e-b969-29c06504b700_900x450.png)

Before you allocate 2027 hours to PR, content, or community, check which brands AI recommends in your category and which sources it cites.

Semrush is sponsoring this week’s memo, and its free[AI Visibility Index](https://ai-visibility-index.semrush.com/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=socialorganic_partners_growthmemo&utm_term=social_organic&utm_content=kevinindig_october05) lets you compare thousands of brands across 22 industries and four AI platforms. Its flagship study draws on 126M+ real AI search prompts.

Use the source data to shortlist places where your team could earn mentions next year, and the accompanying free studies and playbooks to choose tactics to test. Bring that shortlist into your planning meeting: which sources deserve a person’s time, and how many hours can you commit?

This year, if you gave a hefty amount of your planning resources to digital PR, it makes sense: 2025 and 2026 analyses found that it’s crucial to AI visibility. In fact, AirOps found that third-party signals [drive 85% of brand visibility](https://www.airops.com/report/the-influence-of-offsite-signals-in-ai-search) in LLMs.

Natividad extends that line past earned third-party signals:

> _“Budget for creating and distributing content beyond your own website, and actually engage with those communities. Then focus on creating ideas worth talking about, that also get mentioned and cited by other credible sources, and showing up in the places where people are already having relevant conversations.”_

Community participation is labor, and should be planned for accordingly. And a [community or UGC line](https://library.growth-memo.com/p/user-generated-content-ugc) with no named owner is the first one cut when Q2 gets tight, so budget it as hours per week with a person attached.

“Ideas worth talking about,” as Amanda mentioned, is a research cost. In 2027, fund the proprietary data that gives other sources a reason to cite you, the core of the[brand authority series](https://www.growth-memo.com/p/multiply-your-brand-authority). Community expenses can be folded into the same capacity line item as SEO because its cost is pretty much fixed. Spend 5% (maybe 10% in some cases) of your marketing budget on community. (There’s [a slide deck](https://members.growth-memo.com/resources/brand-authority-multiplication-deck) in the [premium library](https://members.growth-memo.com/resources/brand-authority-multiplication-deck) to help explain this concept of brand authority multiplication to your team.)

Natividad’s measurement advice starts where attribution stops:

> _“Measurement has to expand, too. Look at search and AI visibility, citations and mentions, but also platform signals like impressions, engagement, branded search, and eventually conversions. None of those metrics individually proves that you influenced someone. But together, they give you a much better picture of whether your brand is actually reaching people.”_

Last week’s memo on[the collapse of attribution](https://growth-memo.com/p/the-collapse-of-attribution) called this triangulation:

> Combine three signals with different blind spots: an exposure metric, a behavioral signal, and a business outcome. For AI visibility, that could mean Share of Voice, self-reported discovery or CRM tags, and conversions; confidence rises when they move together, while divergence tells you where to investigate.

Natividad’s own recommended list maps onto 3 layers:

[![Image 5](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!9vzw!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F825f41d8-ff52-4c8d-8750-885bb1b253ef_2048x1673.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!9vzw!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F825f41d8-ff52-4c8d-8750-885bb1b253ef_2048x1673.png)

Report all 3 layers on the same page every month. A few examples:

*   **Exposure up, but branded search flat.** Mentions aren’t landing with buyers. A distribution problem: move content and participation into the communities and channels your audience uses.

*   **Branded search up, pipeline flat.** People went looking and didn’t convert. This is a conversion problem: Fix the pages they land on, the offer, or the handoff to sales.

*   **Branded search up, direct visits up, AI citations flat.** Something off-site is working (a podcast, an event, a partner, word of mouth) and AI hasn’t caught up. Find the source and fund more like it.

*   **Exposure and branded search both down.** Someone else is taking the mentions. This is a competitor problem: Audit who AI recommends in your category now and which sources it cites for them.

Each mix of the three layers points to a different fix.

“All of these systems are trying to understand and reflect human behavior,” Natividad shared with me. “Mentions, citations, discussions, engagement, and recommendations are all proxies for real people paying attention.”

And that’s what you need to communicate to the c-suite.

Set your 2027 organic targets as _presence_ on surfaces where your audience is and your potential buyers are researching. Develop goals to build:

1/ Visibility with [AI engines](https://library.growth-memo.com/p/answer-engine) your customers actually use

2/ Authority with online communities and publications where your category gets discussed, and

3/ Organic branded search volume.

Last year, we were all working to sell experiments to our leadership teams. Your 2027 plan, however, needs 3 separate “buckets” of work that you’re resourcing, each with its own rules:

*   Proven work, funded at full capacity: The tactics (born out of 2026’s learnings) that are providing you competitive growth in your vertical, along with technical SEO, content refreshes, and the digital PR that already earns citations.

*   Learning work, capped with one owner and a kill date: AI marketing team automation pilots and new search surfaces you haven’t tested.

*   Unmeasurable bets, funded on judgment: community, events, and brand work tests. Ramp’s George Bonaci[said in last week’s memo](https://growth-memo.com/p/the-collapse-of-attribution) that attribution alone “would have led us to cancel all brand marketing, stunts, direct mail, events.”

Current search volatility argues for shorter commitments, so lock the annual budgeting total you can work from, and re-split the buckets every quarter against the 3-layer measurement set. The Growth Memo premium library has the [SEO budget planning tool](https://members.growth-memo.com/resources/seo-budget-planner) to help you build the case.

I would recommend quarterly re-forecasting, and many of the CMOs that I work with are comfortable with this regular reevaluation of resourcing. Ultimately, your team needs the freedom to adapt as things move _before_ the next biannual or annual budget planning.

Directors who walk into 2027 planning without a defensible AI SEO investment case will lose budget to paid. But you don’t have to.

kept.heading: PERFORMANCE MAX AND ADVANTAGE+ GRADE THEIR OWN HOMEWORK (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Meta Advantage+ and Google Performance Max should be treated as optimization tools, not independent proof of advertising impact, because the platforms control buying, attribution, and reporting. Optmyzr found Performance Max overlapped with existing Search keywords in 91% of 503 Google Ads accounts. The same problem appears in Meta and Google reporting because platforms can count modeled conversions and prioritize brand searches, existing customers, and other users who were already likely to convert. When making budget decisions, rely on randomized incrementality tests, auditable holdouts, finance reconciliations, and visibility into what the system actually bought rather than platform-reported ROAS alone.

Title: Performance Max and Advantage+ Grade Their Own Homework

URL Source: https://karandhir.substack.com/p/performance-max-and-advantage-grade

Published Time: 2026-10-07T18:02:04+00:00

Markdown Content:
In July, Meta told investors that its Advantage+ products had passed a $75 billion annual revenue run rate. Meta’s total revenue that quarter was $60.8 billion, so the automated products now carry close to a third of the company’s revenue pace. Three years earlier, in the third quarter of 2023, Mark Zuckerberg had told the same investors that Advantage+ Shopping was at a $10 billion run rate. By the fourth quarter of 2024 it was past $20 billion, up 70% in a year, and in early 2025 Meta renamed the product Advantage+ Sales and widened it to leads and app installs. The growth from $10 billion to $75 billion came from advertisers handing the buying decisions to the platform, one campaign at a time, because the dashboard said it was working.

Google took the same path with Performance Max. Since its launch in November 2021, one Performance Max campaign has been able to spend across Search, Shopping, YouTube, Display, Discover, Gmail and Maps from a single budget, with the system deciding the split. For most of that time the advertiser could not see the split. Channel-level reporting only arrived in 2025, and full campaign-level negative keywords only arrived in 2026, more than four years after launch. For four years, the largest ad platform in the world asked advertisers to fund a machine that would not say where the money went, and most of them funded it anyway, because the reported returns looked strong.

I want to make one argument this week, and it is simpler than the technology around it. These systems bid toward the conversions their own models count, and then they report on those same counts. The seller of the media runs the buying, counts the results, and writes the report card. No supplier in any other category gets that arrangement from a serious finance team. Ad platforms get it from marketing teams every day, and the reason is that the report card looks good.

Strip away the product names and here is what you are doing when you launch an automated campaign. You hand the platform a goal, usually purchases or leads, along with a budget and a pile of creative. The system then decides who sees the ads, where, when, and at what price. It learns from the conversions it counts. The word counts is doing the work in that sentence, because the machine does not learn from your sales ledger. It learns from pixel events, server events sent through a conversions API, modeled conversions that fill privacy gaps, and attribution windows the platform sets. A purchase that your finance team records once can appear as a conversion in two platforms, or in neither, depending on what each platform’s tracking saw and what each one chose to model.

The modeled share of those counts is larger than most budget owners realize. After Apple’s App Tracking Transparency arrived in April 2021 and cut off much of the tracking on iPhones, Meta told advertisers that September that it believed it was underreporting iOS web conversions by about 15%, and it filled the gap with statistical modeling. Those modeled events sit in the same column as observed ones, feed the same bidding system, and roll up into the same return on ad spend figure that reaches the budget meeting. A number that is partly estimated is still presented as a count.

The latitude the machine has is also larger than most people assume. Google’s own help documentation states that a campaign may spend up to twice its average daily budget on any given day, with a monthly cap of 30.4 times the daily figure. That is a rule about pace, and it is a reasonable one. There is no comparable rule in the product about what the spend is allowed to buy. The system can decide that your brand name is the best keyword in the account, that your existing customers are the best audience, and that a placement you have never heard of is the best inventory, and it will be right by its own scorecard every time, because the scorecard is the one it wrote.

In 2019, Marketing Science published a study by Brett Gordon, Florian Zettelmeyer, Neha Bhargava and Dan Chapsky that used Facebook’s own experimentation system. They took 15 large randomized experiments, covering 500 million user-experiment observations and 1.6 billion ad impressions, and treated the randomized results as the truth. Then they asked how close the standard observational methods came. Those methods, including exact matching, propensity scores and regression adjustment, often overstated the incremental conversions by a factor of three or more, sometimes understated them, and gave no reliable way to know in advance which direction the error would run. Gordon, Robert Moakler and Zettelmeyer repeated the exercise across hundreds of experiments in 2023 and reached the same conclusion.

Here is why that matters for automated buying specifically. The reason observational methods fail is that ad systems show ads to people who were already likely to convert, and no amount of adjustment on what you can observe removes a selection process running on what you cannot. An automated bidding system is that selection process, built on purpose and improving every week. Its entire job is to find the people closest to converting and to pay for their attention, and then it counts their conversions and calls the count performance. The better the machine gets at its job, the less its own counts prove, because the gap between people who converted after seeing the ad and people who would have converted anyway is exactly the gap the machine is paid to close.

The clearest public evidence comes from the people who manage these accounts at scale. In February 2025, Optmyzr reviewed a month of data across 503 Google Ads accounts to see how Performance Max interacts with the Search campaigns running beside it. In 91% of those accounts, Performance Max was serving on search terms that already had a matching keyword in a Search campaign. In a second cut across 511 accounts, 97% showed search term overlap between the two campaign types, across 424,820 terms. At the time of the study, Google did not report cost data for Performance Max search terms, so Optmyzr could not compare cost per acquisition or return on ad spend between the two. That sentence deserves a second read, because it describes the normal state of a large account: the agency could see that the machine was buying the same searches twice, and could not see what it paid.

The reason this matters goes back to eBay. In 2012, eBay shut off paid search for its own brand name in about 30% of US markets for 60 days, and found the channel was producing close to zero incremental sales. Econometrica published the result in 2015. Brand searches convert well because the person had already decided. An automated system that is scored on conversions will find brand searches first, because they are the cheapest conversions in the account, and it will then report those conversions as performance. Nothing in that chain is dishonest. The machine did what it was built to do, the report describes what was counted, and what was counted was mostly demand you already had.

Adidas learned the same thing the slow way. Simon Peel, the company’s global media director, told the EffWeek conference in 2019 that Adidas had been running four attribution systems at once, from Google, Adobe and Facebook, and that all four agreed that lower-funnel digital was driving the business. When a technical fault stopped paid search in Latin America in 2017, traffic and revenue barely moved. An econometric model later found that brand activity, which had been getting 23% of the budget, was driving 65% of sales, and Adidas moved from a 77/23 performance and brand split to roughly 60/40 the other way. Four reports from four vendors had agreed with each other and been wrong in the same direction, because all four were counting the same observable clicks.

Meta’s automation has the same shape with different controls. An Advantage+ sales campaign lets you set a cap on how much of the budget goes to existing customers, and that cap is close to the full extent of the mandate you give it. The system decides audiences, placements across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and the Audience Network, and the creative combinations it serves. Meta reports that its automated campaigns deliver lower cost per purchase than manual ones, and I have no reason to doubt the comparison. The comparison is still measured on Meta’s counts, by Meta’s attribution, inside Meta’s reporting. It tells you the machine beats a human at the game the platform scores, and it tells you nothing about what the game is worth.

I have sat across the table from platform measurement teams for years, and I have never met one I thought was lying. That is exactly the point, and it is why I frame this as a design problem. A company that sells media, operates the buying system, counts the conversions and writes the reporting has a conflict of interest that no individual’s integrity can resolve, because the conflict lives in the product. It shows up in which numbers are easy to see and which take four years to ship. It shows up in which studies are one click away and which require a sales call. It shows up in the word performance sitting on top of a column of modeled events. The people are fine, the arrangement is the problem, and the arrangement persists because the numbers it produces are pleasant to present.

There is one more piece of evidence that the platforms themselves know the difference. In May 2025, Google cut the minimum budget for a randomized incrementality test in Google Ads from about $100,000 to $5,000. A company does not build and discount a product that measures true lift unless it accepts that its default reporting does not. The existence of the test is the platform’s own admission, and it is the cheapest admission you will ever get.

I run measurement for a large marketing portfolio, and my posture toward automated campaigns is classification. I neither trust the reporting nor boycott the products, because the products are good at buying. I classify every number before it enters a budget conversation, and for automated campaigns the classification runs on four questions.

First, was assignment randomized, and by what mechanism? A real lift study can answer this concretely, with a holdout group withheld before the auction. A modeled result cannot answer it, and the vendor’s response will describe adjustment rather than randomization.

Second, who holds the holdout, and can we audit it? Randomization run inside the platform, measured by the platform, and reported by the platform is evidence with a custody problem. Exportable results, pre-agreed statistical power, and third-party measurement partners are what mature arrangements look like.

Third, does the outcome reconcile to anything our finance team recognizes? A conversion count that cannot be walked, even roughly, to a line in the ledger will win the marketing meeting and lose the CFO.

Fourth, and this one is specific to automated buying, what did the machine actually buy? What share of the reported conversions came from brand terms, from existing customers, and from each channel? If the platform cannot answer, then the platform is asking you to grade a report with the questions redacted, and the right response is to budget the campaign accordingly.

The numbers that pass all four questions get treated as evidence and used to calibrate our models. Everything else gets treated as telemetry. Telemetry has real uses in running a campaign day to day, since it tells you the machine is running and roughly how hard. It does not tell you whether the machine is making you money, and a dashboard that says it is should carry the same weight as a contractor’s own invoice marked approved.

The scale here is what makes the question urgent rather than academic. Automated products now carry a $75 billion run rate at one company and the default campaign type at another, and both platforms are asking for more authority every quarter. The newer AI ad surfaces, which I will get to at the end of this month, offer even less visibility than the ones I have described here. You cannot supervise an allocator with the allocator’s own reporting, and that sentence is the whole series.

There is exactly one audit a bidding algorithm cannot argue with, and it is a market that got no ads. Next week I will walk through what Uber, JPMorgan Chase, Procter & Gamble and Airbnb each learned by turning the machines off, and how to build that lesson into a standing line item instead of waiting for a crisis to run the test for you.

kept.heading: PINTEREST LAUNCHES BEAUTY GUIDES TO TURN INSPIRATION INTO ACTION (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Tapping "Get the Guide" on a hair or nail Pin now generates a personalized guide for recreating the look. Pinterest's visual understanding tech identifies details like hairstyle, color, nail shape, and finish, then an LLM turns them into salon talking points, step-by-step instructions, and relevant products.
kept.article_text:
Title: Pinterest launches Beauty Guides to turn inspiration into action

URL Source: https://newsroom.pinterest.com/news/pinterest-launches-beauty-guides-to-turn-inspiration-into-action/

Published Time: 2026-10-06

Markdown Content:
Beauty inspiration should be more than a screenshot you hope to find again before your next appointment.

Today, Pinterest is launching Beauty Guides, a new AI powered experience that turns hair and nail Pins into personalized, actionable guides designed to help people recreate the looks they discover on Pinterest.

Beauty Guides use Pinterest’s visual understanding technology to analyze a look in a Pin, identifying details such as hairstyle, color, nail shape and finish. That visual understanding is combined with a large language model to turn what you see on Pinterest into a useful guide for real life, including what to ask for at the salon, what to expect during an appointment, similar looks to explore, relevant products and set by step instructions.

When users open a hair or nail Pin in closeup, they can tap “**Get the Guide”** to access their guide and save it for their next appointment or use it to recreate the look at home.

The experience addresses a familiar challenge in beauty discovery—people often know exactly what they want when they see it, even if they do not have the words to describe it. Beauty Guides help bridge that gap by understanding the image itself and translating visual inspiration into something people can act on.

“People come to Pinterest with a point of view, even if they don’t know the words to describe it,” said Matt Madrigal, Chief Product and Technology Officer Pinterest. “Beauty Guides use our visual understanding technology and AI to help people go from seeing a look they love to knowing how to make it their own, whether that means knowing what to ask for at the salon, finding the right products or recreating the look at home.”

### **From seeing something you love to knowing what to do next**

Pinterest is a visual search and shopping platform built for the moments when people are deciding what to try, buy or do next.

Those journeys do not always begin with words. They often begin with an image, feeling or something that catches your eye.

Beauty Guides show how Pinterest can use AI to make those visual journeys more actionable. By combining visual understanding with generative AI, Pinterest can understand the details within an image and transform them into guidance people can use in the real world.

It is one example of **Pinterest Intelligence,**the system that brings together Pinterest’s first party signals, visual understanding technology and purpose built AI models to power more personalized and actionable experiences across the platform.

Instead of stopping at “**I love that,**” Pinterest can help people get to “**I know what to do next**.”

### **The place where beauty discovery starts**

Among weekly Pinterest users who have made beauty purchases, Pinterest is already where people actively plan what's next in beauty. More than 85% of Pinterest users say they discover new beauty trends and ideas on Pinterest before seeing them anywhere else.1 That discovery feels personal—compared with the competitive average, users are 79% more likely to say Pinterest's beauty content feels extremely relevant to them, including ideas that reflect their own skin tone and hair type.2 And when inspiration turns into intent, people trust Pinterest to help them decide what to try next: nearly nine in 10 Pinterest users say they feel confident buying beauty products they discover on the platform.3

Beauty Guides is now available to iOS users in the U.S., with plans to expand to more people and regions over time, as well as to introduce guides across additional product categories.

kept.article_text:
Title: Brands Using Packaging To Disrupt An Industry

URL Source: https://thebrandblueprint.substack.com/p/brands-using-packaging-to-disrupt

Published Time: 2026-10-07T13:09:57+00:00

Markdown Content:
[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!FqA7!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fed98ab92-54ff-465e-89f6-257ddd45b12f_1920x1080.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!FqA7!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fed98ab92-54ff-465e-89f6-257ddd45b12f_1920x1080.png)

Happy Wednesday!

I hope everyone is having a great week!

Today’s post is inspired by this [new soap brand](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92173753) started by three former executives at Bubble.

They thought they were disrupting the soap industry for Gen Z with their cringe branding, but really it’s just a brand full of misconceptions about Gen Z.

I actually think their “disruptive” branding is more destructive to the brand than anything else.

I think a lot of new brands fall into one of two camps: they’re either really good at using packaging and branding to disrupt an industry, or they completely drop the ball.

So I wanted to talk about some of my favorite brands that are actually using packaging to disrupt an industry.

Let’s talk about it.

P.S. I made a [list](https://amzn.to/43FRq0s) of all my favorite **[Amazon Prime Sales](https://amzn.to/43FRq0s)** happening today. Also Hill House just dropped the [coolest outfits](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92409684) for the holiday season.

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!w9-O!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F520cf97b-60e8-440b-9c63-fcedf2f3fa0e_1920x1080.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!w9-O!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F520cf97b-60e8-440b-9c63-fcedf2f3fa0e_1920x1080.png)

Packaging is one of the few marketing channels that keeps working after someone buys the product.

If something looks good enough to leave out on the counter, it gets seen every day. If it photographs well, customers naturally post it on social media. And if it looks completely different from everything around it in retail, the packaging can get someone to discover the brand before they know anything else about it.

That is basically free marketing built into the product.

And good packaging can do even more than generate awareness. It can change what people think a category is worth, make a product easier to use, or make something people normally hide away feel worthy of being displayed.

That’s why I think packaging can genuinely change the trajectory of a brand.

The goal isn’t just to make something that looks cool. The packaging should give customers a reason to notice, remember, or share the product differently.

So lets talk about my favorite brands doing that.

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ulOS!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F5a6ac410-458b-407e-a6fd-aa1219900f2e_1414x610.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ulOS!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F5a6ac410-458b-407e-a6fd-aa1219900f2e_1414x610.png)

Boxed wine has traditionally been treated like the less premium alternative to bottled wine, and the packaging hasn’t done much to change that perception.

**[Juliet](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410284)** does the opposite.

Instead of another rectangular carton, the brand uses tall cylindrical containers with bold colors, oversized typography, and minimal graphics. It feels closer to something you would find in beauty or home design than the boxed wine aisle.

Packaging changes the way customers perceive the value of the product before they even taste it.

By removing the visual cues people associate with cheap boxed wine, **[Juliet](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410284)** makes the entire format feel more elevated. The packaging itself becomes part of why someone notices it, displays it, and potentially shares it.

*   Could changing your packaging challenge a negative perception customers already have about your category?

[![Image 4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!yHGF!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe9e7f524-4cc2-47df-9656-4dca6bc50f33_1360x610.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!yHGF!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe9e7f524-4cc2-47df-9656-4dca6bc50f33_1360x610.png)

Cocktail mixers have traditionally been bulky bottles that live in the fridge or behind a bar.

**[Craftmix](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410488)** completely changes where the product can go by turning cocktail mix into small, single-serve packets.

You can throw one in your purse or suitcase, add it to water, and suddenly make a cocktail or mocktail almost anywhere.

Packaging can expand the situations where someone thinks to buy or use something.

A traditional cocktail mixer is mostly an at-home product. [Craftmix](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410488) can be used while traveling, at a picnic, at a party, or anywhere else you can find water.

*   Is your current packaging limiting where and when customers can use your product?

[![Image 5](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ks8W!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F1f9175ca-d294-4626-b38b-00784a6b0c51_1348x614.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ks8W!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F1f9175ca-d294-4626-b38b-00784a6b0c51_1348x614.png)

Olive oil has traditionally been sold through old-world cues: dark glass bottles, narrow necks, traditional labels, and lots of language around heritage and provenance.

**[Graza](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410751)** made the category feel completely different.

The brand uses colorful squeeze bottles that feel more like a kitchen tool than a precious pantry item. Even the names “Sizzle” and “Drizzle” make it obvious what each oil is supposed to be used for.

[Graza](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410751) created packaging customers have a functional reason to prefer.

The squeeze bottle makes olive oil easier to cook with while also creating a silhouette you can recognize from across a kitchen or grocery aisle. It solves a usability problem and builds brand recognition at the same time.

*   Could your packaging make the product easier or more enjoyable to use?

[![Image 6](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!OG6A!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8de39439-f5fe-457d-936a-78ec32a342b0_1350x612.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!OG6A!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8de39439-f5fe-457d-936a-78ec32a342b0_1350x612.png)

Dry shampoo has basically looked and worked the same way for years: a colorful aerosol can you spray into your hair between washes.

**[Crown Affair](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410664)**[](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410664)changes the entire experience.

Its dry shampoo comes in a minimal black-and-white jar with a brush used to apply the powder directly to your roots. The product feels much closer to makeup or skincare than traditional dry shampoo.

Packaging influences how people use a product and, in turn, how valuable that product feels.

Applying dry shampoo with a brush feels more controlled and intentional than spraying an aerosol can. [Crown Affair](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410664)uses the packaging to make a familiar category feel more elevated.

*   Could changing the way customers apply your product change how they value it?

[![Image 7](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!1w2B!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3f9bde65-c9a7-4131-8ca8-995401d77e04_1368x604.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!1w2B!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3f9bde65-c9a7-4131-8ca8-995401d77e04_1368x604.png)

Sleep supplements usually look like supplements.

Plastic bottles, dark colors, moon graphics, and labels filled with dosages, ingredients, and sleep claims have become the default language of the category.

**[Sleep or Die](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410594)** completely breaks from that.

Instead of another bottle of gummies or capsules, the product comes in individually packaged dissolvable strips with bold red branding and a name that is almost impossible to forget.

A new format gives customers something new to notice and talk about.

The strips are portable and easy to use, but they also give [Sleep or Die](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410594) a product experience that looks and feels completely different from the rest of the category.

*   Does your product actually need to come in the same format as every competitor?

[![Image 8](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!kxWJ!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F5e04acd7-a221-4553-bed4-18662fece1f8_1358x606.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!kxWJ!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F5e04acd7-a221-4553-bed4-18662fece1f8_1358x606.png)

Peanut butter packaging has barely changed, even though natural peanut butter has one annoying problem: you have to stir it.

**[One Trick Pony](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410345)** flips the jar upside down to make the product easier to stir and use.

That one decision also makes the brand immediately look different on shelf. Before you even notice the bright green packaging or read the name, the jar is sitting differently from every peanut butter around it.

The packaging solves a product problem while creating visual differentiation at the same time. That is a much stronger reason to be different than changing a label simply for the sake of standing out.

*   What frustration has your category accepted for years that packaging could actually solve?

[![Image 9](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!RIQf!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd9f5e905-b2eb-4db5-bc9e-9ba91e41f130_1400x616.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!RIQf!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fd9f5e905-b2eb-4db5-bc9e-9ba91e41f130_1400x616.png)

Makeup wipes typically come in one large resealable pouch, which makes perfect sense when the product lives in your bathroom.

**[4AM](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410818)** designed its packaging around all the moments when it doesn’t.

Its Clean Sheets are individually wrapped, serum-infused wipes that can live in a purse, gym bag, suitcase, or nightstand. Instead of positioning them as another basic makeup wipe, the brand describes them as essentially an entire skincare routine in a wipe.

[4AM](https://go.shopmy.us/p-92410818) built the package around the moments customers are most likely to need the product: late nights, travel, workouts, or anytime doing a full skincare routine feels unrealistic.

*   Is your packaging designed around where customers actually need the product?

There’s a big difference between packaging that looks disruptive and packaging that actually changes how people use or perceive a product.

The strongest brands are doing more than making packaging look cool. They’re making products easier to use, more display-worthy, and more likely to be shared.

And when packaging can do all of that, it stops being decoration and starts becoming a real marketing channel.

Have a great rest of your week!

-Brooke

kept.heading: GLASTONBURY VS THE INTERNET: WHAT R/GLASTONBURY_FESTIVAL DID WHEN TICKETS SOLD OUT (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Glastonbury's Reddit community shows how brands can turn high-stress moments into stronger loyalty by giving people a place to share experiences and help each other. After tickets sold out in 42 minutes, the subreddit created a dedicated thread for winners and naturally enforced norms that kept celebrations from alienating people who missed out. Roughly one in six comments focused on missing confirmation emails, yet experienced ticket buyers quickly answered questions and reassured anxious strangers. The result was a community that provided practical support, shared expertise, and even connected strangers who ended up buying tickets and attending the festival together.
kept.article_text:
Title: Glastonbury Reddit: What Fans Did When Tickets Sold Out - Standing on Giants

URL Source: https://www.standingongiants.com/blog/glastonbury-reddit-tickets-sold-out/

Markdown Content:
## **So what happened?**

Glastonbury 2027 tickets went on sale at 9am on Sunday. By 9:42 they were gone.

42 minutes.

That’s after a fallow year, at £408 a ticket, with a registration system so tight you have to enter your mates’ details before you’re even allowed in the queue. Weeks of group chats and spreadsheets of registration numbers. Then 42 minutes, and for most people, nothing.

Glastonbury ticket morning is one of the great shared rituals of British internet life, and Reddit is where people go to process it. So I spent the evening reading the comments in the r/glastonbury_festival thread. The mods were ready…

They put up a megathread called “I GOT TICKETS” with a short note at the top: “People are obviously emotional if they miss out, and it’s not fair to rub it in their faces.” If you got a ticket, keep the chat in here.

And people respected it. One first-timer admitted they’d already posted their own celebration thread, then deleted it when they spotted the megathread. No moderator had to ask. They were “just pretty excited and got carried away haha.”

The very first comment in the I Got Tickets thread was from someone who hadn’t got tickets. We’ll come back to them.

![Image 1](https://www.standingongiants.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/lee-blanchflower-1dW1vEJLlCQ-unsplash-1024x683.jpg)

Shared goals, instant community.

## **Ten years, a bus and a Greggs in Tenerife**

Most of the thread is a roll call of stubbornness. Ten years of trying came up three separate times. Eight years. Five years. “Haven’t been since 2017, tried every year since and failed, but we got them this morning.”

One group of five, all first-timers, finally got through after a decade of failing. Their method was to log on at 8:20 and “just didn’t touch the screen.” Their verdict: “Really does feel like pure luck.”

What struck me is that almost nobody was sat calmly at a desk. Someone got through from a bus on the way to brunch, on “dodgy 5G”, inside the first five minutes. Someone else forgot the sale was even happening, woke up to a reminder text with 20% battery, no bank card and nobody’s registration details to hand, and still sorted it in under five minutes: “I feel so lucky I never have good luck.”

My favourite, from a first-time buyer who got through on their first attempt: “Literally in Tenerife Airport Greggs with 5G and a prayer.”

And then there’s the one who wasn’t even fussed. They joined the queue, left it running in the background and went off to read the news. When they checked back they were on 17 bars (the progress bar everyone stares at for an hour). The reaction was a quiet “holy sh*t”. They asked their girlfriend if she fancied it. She “weighed it up and said ‘yeah, go on then.'”

Thousands of people would have traded anything for that queue position. They got it while doing something else.

At the other end of the commitment scale, one commenter listed 18 Coachellas, three Bonnaroos, Electric Forest and Primavera Sound, and was “finally” heading to Worthy Farm with a crew of 26. It was the most upvoted comment in the thread. “Ecstatic is an understatement.”

![Image 2](https://www.standingongiants.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/joe-green-9ZCZoH69dZQ-unsplash-1024x768.jpg)

**Arcadia spider:**_Built from recycled military scrap._

## **“It pays to have friendless friends”**

Glastonbury tickets are bought in groups of up to six. Everyone pools their registration numbers, everyone queues, and whoever gets through first buys for the group. Which turns ticket morning into a pretty brutal test of friendship.

The best version of it: one commenter’s mate got within three bars of the front before the tickets sold out. Gutted. Then it turned out another friend, a first-timer, had quietly put the commenter in their group (“can’t remember agreeing to that…”) and got through. “It pays to have friendless friends (love you mate).”

The worst version is harder to read. One lead booker hit an error at checkout because a friend’s postcode didn’t match his registration. With minutes left and no reply to calls or messages, they swapped him out for someone else and bought the tickets. “Obviously he’s fuming.” Underneath, a stranger admitted doing exactly the same thing: “Feel bad but there’s not much you can do.”

One mate left their group the night before to join a different group of six. The new group didn’t get through. The original group did. “I just wish they’d never switched,” wrote someone in the same position, “(they’ll be kicking themselves the most though).”

Then there’s the guilt of getting lucky. The person who got through on the bus only had their own details and their cousin’s, so they could only buy two tickets. “I’m feeling so guilty for not asking more friends for their details but there was no time.” They signed off with: “I feel like can’t even tell anyone we got ours lol.”

Not everyone was carrying it quite so heavily. “8 years of trying, finally going! 6 of our 12 man group missed out sadly but sucks to be them I guess.”

And when one commenter said a friend had forgotten to add their sister, so they’d have to sell their ticket, the reply came back fast: “Sell? I’ve got news for you buddy…” (Glastonbury tickets carry your photo and can’t be resold, outside the official resale.)

## “Anyone else not got their confirmation email yet?”

Getting a ticket, it turns out, is only the first half of the anxiety. The second half is waiting for the email.

Roughly one in six comments in the thread were about confirmation emails. People posted their booking times like flight numbers. “Got my tickets at like 9.38 for reference.” “That’s almost the exact time I got mine, no email yet.” Someone booking from Australia wondered if the time difference was the problem. Someone else just wrote “Getting STRESSED.”

Nobody from the festival or the ticket company was in the thread. Nobody needed to be. The most useful comment came from a fellow ticket holder who’d been through it before. Emails can take up to 24 hours. As long as you reached the screen listing who you’d paid deposits for, it’ll come. And if you want proof now, get your lead booker to check their bank account for a £600 deposit with “TICKETS” in the reference.

“Thanks for this, has put my mind at ease somewhat!!!”

Then, one by one, the replies started to resolve themselves. “Edit: Just came in!” “Panic over, email has arrived.” The Australian, mid-conversation with a stranger in London who’d told them “Thousands in the same boat mate”, interrupted with: “Well speaking of, I just got my confirmation!”

It’s the least dramatic part of the thread, and the bit I’d show to anyone who doubts what a community is for. A thread full of strangers, holding each other’s hands through a refresh button.

![Image 3](https://www.standingongiants.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/tijs-van-leur-So6YckShOVA-unsplash-scaled.jpg)

## **“Ten years of working in ticketing here”**

The second most upvoted comment wasn’t a celebration at all. It was someone who has worked in ticketing for a decade, reverse engineering the system in real time.

Their group’s lead booker had bought six tickets and been sent straight back to the front of the queue, which has happened for years. He tried to buy six more for other friends and got blocked at checkout. Their theory: each booking is now tied to the lead booker’s registration. In past years, they said, once you were through you could go back in and buy as many orders of six as you liked. This year, that door seems to have been shut, which would explain why registrations now have to be entered before you join the queue.

Then they asked the question everyone in their position wanted answering. Can I still use my registration in the April resale to help friends, now it’s attached to a ticket?

Strangers chipped in with what they’d seen. One had bought a coach ticket on Thursday and found their registration wouldn’t even let them into Sunday’s queue. Another said a friend had tried to buy for a second group and been refused.

And then the ticketing veteran spotted the weak point: if registrations can only be used once, people who are registered but not going could start selling their numbers to people who want extra places in the queue. “The new system has felt really fair so far, but that could be a weak spot.”

None of this is confirmed by the festival or See Tickets. It’s a group of strangers comparing notes, and a couple of people were convinced of glitches that may or may not exist. But the mood was striking for a sale where most people lose. “It does seem fairer,” wrote one commenter, who’d watched what they called the “green bar of doom” and come out the other side with tickets.

![Image 4](https://www.standingongiants.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/anthony-delanoix-hzgs56Ze49s-unsplash-1-1024x683.jpg)

Strangers, briefly on the same side.

## **“Can’t believe my sesh head mate missed out to a 13 year old”**

The sweetest exchange in the thread started with a parent who’d got tickets for themselves and their 13-year-old daughter. They’re planning to keep it secret until Christmas. 2027 is probably the last year they can get away with taking her out of school for things like this, so they’re doing Primavera Sound and Glastonbury in the same June.

A stranger from earlier in the thread, the one whose mate fell three bars short, replied: “Can’t believe my sesh head mate missed out to a 13 year old.”

The parent came straight back. Someone has to make sure “the future generation of sesh heads know how to behave at gigs and festivals”, so really this is a public service. “i’ll make sure she is fully aware of who had to be sacrificed for her to go.”

Then a foster parent joined in. They’d got tickets too, for their foster son’s first big festival and first time seeing artists live, and they were already picturing him walking into Arcadia (the giant fire-breathing spider of a stage, for the uninitiated). Mid-comment, panic: he might be in the middle of exams. A quick search later, relief. He finishes five days before. “What a way to celebrate.”

Two strangers, cheering on each other’s kids.

The first-timers were everywhere. Someone flying in from Australia. Someone going solo. A first-timer going with their partner, asking how you make festival friends. A fifth-timer bringing a whole group who’d never been. A group of five, all going for the first time, together, after a decade of trying.

![Image 5](https://www.standingongiants.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/tijs-van-leur-Qnlp3FCO2vc-unsplash-1-1024x683.jpg)

Worth every refresh

## **The people who didn’t get tickets**

Back to that first comment.

The moderators had built a room for the winners, and the first person through the door was someone who’d lost. “Seriously depressed. Missed out.” They’d been the last two years and felt lucky for it. But it was only now sinking in how much those five days meant. “It is the only time I can take a break and properly enjoy myself without issues of work, family, commitments etc.”

And then, instead of resentment: “I hope there are a lot of 1st timers going next year, who are finally able to experience the magic of Glastonbury and why it is different from every other festival. Hope you all have a brilliant time.”

They signed off with the best line in the whole thread. “I’m off to research about excavating to try and take my mind off things.”

I have no idea what that means. I love it anyway.

They weren’t the only one. “I didn’t get through but I am particularly pleased for all the first-timers I’m seeing,” wrote another. “Your first time is unforgettable!” A group of 15 across three queues, none of whom got closer than five and a half bars, got a last-minute message from a friend of a friend who was at checkout with four spare places. “So at least 4 of us get to go again.”

And for balance, because this is still Reddit: one commenter posted “Sixth year in a row with nothing, never been and probably never will.” The only reply: “On the plus side you haven’t lost anything.”

The comment I keep coming back to, though, is a short one. “I just got mine for me, my husband and 3 other people we met in this group!”

They’d met on the subreddit. Then they queued together. Now they’re going to Glastonbury together.

The moderators built a room for the people who got lucky. The best comments in it came from the people who didn’t.

kept.article_text:
Title: Google Email Shares Number Of Preferred Source Subscribers

URL Source: https://www.seroundtable.com/google-preferred-source-subscribers-email-42244.html

Published Time: 2026-10-06T12:15:00-04:00

Markdown Content:
[Home](https://www.seroundtable.com/) / [Google News](https://www.seroundtable.com/category/google) / [Google Email Shares Number Of Preferred Source Subscribers](https://www.seroundtable.com/google-preferred-source-subscribers-email-42244.html)

![Image 1: Google Source Card](https://images.seroundtable.com/google-source-card-u6Kktsqs.jpg)

Google Search Console is sending out emails informing site owners how many people are subscribing or following them as a [preferred source](https://www.seroundtable.com/google-top-stories-preferred-sources-live-39920.html) on Google. It says "people are choosing domain as a preferred source" and then lists the number of "Preferred source selections."

Here is a screenshot of the email I just received for a random Search Console profile I have access to:

[![Image 2: Google Preferred Source Email Data](https://images.seroundtable.com/google-preferred-source-email-data-0nA7nwyG.png)](https://images.seroundtable.com/google-preferred-source-email-data-0nA7nwyG.png)

It says:

> People are choosing domain as a preferred source
> To the owner of domain:
> 
> 
> Preferred sources lets Google Search users choose the publications they want to see most. When readers select your site, your content can appear more often across features like Top Stories, AI Overviews, and AI Mode.
> 
> 
> Here’s your latest preferred sources data as of 2026-10-05:
> 
> 
> Property name: domain Preferred source selections: ####

It then adds:

Recommended actions

To help your audience add your site as a preferred source, add our interactive button directly to your web pages.

*   Install the JavaScript button: Add two lines of HTML to your site to embed the interactive button. Install the JavaScript button
*   Upgrade existing buttons: Switch to the JavaScript button so that users can add your site in fewer steps if you’re currently using the static image button.

Take a 2-minute survey to help us shape preferred sources reporting in Search Console.

The survey asks:

*   Prior to this report, were you aware of “Preferred Sources,” which lets users choose their favorite sources to show up more often on Google? 
*   How clear was the email in explaining what “Preferred Source user count” means?
*   How helpful is it to know how many users have chosen your site as a "Preferred Source"?
*   If Preferred Sources reporting were provided, how would you prefer to receive it?
*   If Preferred Sources reports were emailed in the future, how frequently would you want to receive email updates on user counts?
*   If Preferred Sources reporting were included in Search Console, which metrics would be most valuable for your site? Please rank your choices in order of value (1 = Most valuable to 4 = Least valuable)
*   Are there any other metrics related to Preferred Sources that would be valuable to your site?

These emails are going out now, it is probably worth filling out the survey so that Google can build the tools we want for preferred sources.

Here are more who spotted this:

Forum discussion at [X](https://x.com/KyleW_Sutton/status/2107492535014949189).

Copied!

Title: Fake influencers, real money: Inside the AI creator business

URL Source: https://mashable.com/life/ai-influencers-business-creators-comedians

Published Time: 2026-10-06T20:35:51+00:00

Markdown Content:
The people on screen don’t exist. But the businesses behind them — and the creators whose work gets copied — do.

![Image 1: artificial intelligence generated image of Aitana Lopez model displayed in a screen at the headquarters of The Clueless company in Barcelona. Described as "strong" and "determined" by Spanish advertising agency The Clueless which offers her services to promote various products, influencer Aitana is not a real person, but an image produced by AI, and a new rival on the influencers' market.](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/01zORhTfwmNIHkYWXtGPZUX/hero-image.fill.size_1248x702.v1791314015.jpg)

Credit: Pau Barrena/Getty Images

You don’t need to be a model to land a brand deal. You don’t need to step onstage to post a stand-up clip. And in the AI influencer business, the person attracting all that attention doesn’t even need to exist.

If you haven’t encountered one yet, an [AI influencer](https://mashable.com/tech/synthetic-performer-disclosure-new-york-state-law-first-complaints) is a character whose images or videos are created using artificial intelligence. A person or company gives it a face, a name, and a social media account, then posts as that character. It might appear to be a model, a lifestyle creator, or a stand-up comedian, with followers who can be directed toward brand promotions, products, or paid subscriptions.

The pitch is that you can do all this without getting in front of a camera. With tools that put AI characters into existing footage, you may not even need to film anything.

* * *

["this is like ecom in 2016,"](https://x.com/sairahul1/status/2107114837872664744?s=42 "(opens in a new window)") one post declares, comparing it to an early opportunity in online retail. "these AI characters have gotten 100M+ views in only the last couple of days," he adds, "making them is SO easy it feels unfair." Another promises a "you can do it in 5min," ending with "hope you get millions of views with this one."
